purindada.cp: masc. an epithet of the king of Devas.
purindada.p: [ puri + dada + a. Ma, ṭī. Pura + dada + a. Kaccaññaḥ. 526. Rū. 567. ] (pu) Google Translate (1) Buddha. (2) Indra.
pn: Purindada. A name for Sakka, because, as a human being, he bestowed gifts from town to town (pure pure dānaṁ adāsi). SN.i.229; Dhp-a.i.264; cp. Sanskrit Purandara (destroyer of cities).

C: purindada：[m．] an epithet of the king of Devas．
P: Purindada，[distorted fr．Vedic puraṁ-dara，pura+dṛ to break，see darī，thus “breaker of fortresses，” Ep．of Indra （& Agni）．The P．Commentator （VvA．171） of course takes it popularly as “pure dānaṁ dadātī ti Purindado ti vuccati，” thus pure+dā； see also Trenckner，Notes 596； Geiger，P．Gr．§ 443] “townbreaker，” a name of Sakka （Indra） D．II，260； S．I，230； Vv 374，622； PvA．247．（Page 469）

DOP: purindada m. [ cf S. puraṃdara], a name of Sakka; D II 260, 1* (Sakko p’ āga ~o); S I 229, 8 (Sakko bhikkhave devānam indo pubbe manussabhūto samāno pure dānaṃ adāsi tasmā ~o ti vuccati); Vv 62:2 (devatā nu si gandhabbo ādu Sakko ~o); Ja V 139, 16* ; Sadd 378, 3* ; 844, 28 (purasaddassa akārassa iṃ ca hoti, pure dānaṃ dadātī ti ~o).
